title: Primary Function of the Connection
learningObjectives: Identify the selected joint's structural function.
student: What is the primary structural function of the selected bolted joint in the basketball-hoop assembly?
instructor: The bolt group transfers load from the backboard mounting plate into the horizontal support structure while holding the connected parts together.
gradingNotes: Look for load transfer through the selected joint, not a description of the entire hoop.
commonMistakes: Students may incorrectly identify the wall anchors as the selected connection.

title: Assigned External Load
learningObjectives: Identify the prescribed connection load and direction.
student: What load is assigned to the selected connection in the simplified problem?
instructor: An equivalent static downward connection shear V = {{bolt_V}} {{bolt_V_unit}} = {{bolt_load_N}} N is applied to the selected bolt group.

title: Connector Identification
learningObjectives: Identify the connectors included in the local model.
student: Which physical components are treated as the connectors in this problem?
instructor: The {{bolt_n_b}} identical mounting bolts joining the backboard mounting plate to the support-arm bracket are the connectors analyzed.

title: Simplified Load Path
learningObjectives: Trace load through the selected connection.
student: Trace the simplified load path from the rim and backboard through the selected bolts and into the support arm.
instructor: Rim/backboard load → backboard/frame → mounting plate → bolts → support-arm bracket → horizontal support arm.

title: Shear Condition
learningObjectives: Relate connection geometry to shear-plane count.
student: In the assigned model, how many shear planes resist load in each bolt, and what physical motion does the shear model represent?
instructor: Each bolt has ns = {{bolt_n_s}} resisting shear plane(s). For the baseline single-shear model, the two connected parts tend to slide relative to one another across one plane through the smooth bolt shank.
commonMistakes: Do not infer double shear merely because several bolts are present; bolt count and shear-plane count are separate quantities.

title: Included and Excluded Responses
learningObjectives: Distinguish the assigned check from a complete connection design.
student: Which connector response is evaluated, and which important connection effects are deliberately excluded?
instructor: The problem evaluates average direct shear stress and shear yielding in the bolts. It excludes bolt tension, eccentric bolt-group moment, bearing, tear-out, prying, thread-root reduction, preload and slip, fatigue, local plate failure, and wall-anchor behavior.

title: Required Parameters
learningObjectives: Identify the data required for a shear-yield safety check.
student: Identify the assigned quantities needed to evaluate bolt shear safety and size the bolts.
instructor: The required data are V = {{bolt_V}} {{bolt_V_unit}}, nb = {{bolt_n_b}}, ns = {{bolt_n_s}}, d = {{bolt_d}} {{bolt_d_unit}}, Sy = {{bolt_S_y}} {{bolt_S_y_unit}}, and FSreq = {{bolt_FS_req}}.

title: Student-Generated Structural Idealization
learningObjectives: Develop a direct-shear bolt-group idealization from a physical connection.
student: Replace the detailed joint with a rigid connection-plate model. Show the applied vertical connection shear V, the {{bolt_n_b}} identical bolts, equal load sharing, and the {{bolt_n_s}} shear plane(s) through one representative bolt. Label Vb, d, and Ab.
instructor: A correct model shows a rigid plate carrying vertical V, {{bolt_n_b}} identical bolts sharing V equally so Vb = V/nb, and one representative bolt with {{bolt_n_s}} shear plane(s). Label d and Ab = πd2/4.
gradingNotes: Students should construct this idealization before viewing the instructor reference image.

title: Modeling Assumptions
learningObjectives: State assumptions supporting equal direct-shear sharing.
student: State the assumptions used to reduce the real connection to the assigned average direct-shear model.
instructor: Use equivalent static loading, identical bolts, equal load sharing, {{bolt_n_s}} shear plane(s) per bolt, smooth shanks at the planes, and rigid connected plates. Exclude the additional connection effects listed in the scope.

title: Mechanics Analysis Plan
learningObjectives: Plan a complete direct-shear safety and sizing calculation.
student: Before substituting values, outline the calculations needed to check the proposed bolts and determine a minimum required diameter.
instructor: Find the load per bolt; compute the shank area; calculate average shear stress; estimate shear-yield strength using von Mises; calculate allowable shear stress and actual factor of safety; solve for minimum diameter; compare the proposal with that diameter; and state model limitations.

title: Load Carried by One Bolt
learningObjectives: Apply equal load sharing to a bolt group.
student: Assuming equal direct-shear sharing, determine the shear force carried by one bolt.
commonMistakes: Do not divide by the shear-plane count here; ns enters the resisting area for each bolt.

title: Bolt Shear Area
student: Determine the nominal shear area of one bolt and its total resisting area across all assigned shear planes.
instructor: Ab = π({{bolt_d}} mm)2/4 = {{bolt_area_mm2}} mm2. The total resisting area per bolt is nsAb = {{bolt_total_shear_area_per_bolt_mm2}} mm2.

title: Average Bolt Shear Stress
learningObjectives: Calculate average shear stress using N and mm units.
student: Determine the average shear stress in one bolt.

title: Shear-Yield and Allowable Stress
learningObjectives: Estimate shear yield and apply a required factor of safety.
student: Using the tensile yield strength and the von Mises criterion, estimate the bolt shear-yield strength and allowable shear stress.

title: Actual Factor of Safety
learningObjectives: Calculate and interpret a shear-yield factor of safety.
student: Determine the actual factor of safety against the estimated bolt shear-yield strength and compare it with the requirement.

title: Minimum Required Bolt Diameter
learningObjectives: Size a circular connector for average direct shear.
student: Determine the minimum nominal smooth-shank bolt diameter required to satisfy the specified factor of safety.

title: Proposed Bolt Assessment
learningObjectives: Compare a proposed connector size with a calculated minimum.
student: Compare the proposed nominal bolt diameter with the calculated minimum and state whether it is adequate for the assigned direct-shear check.
instructor: The proposed diameter is {{bolt_d}} mm and dmin = {{bolt_d_min_mm}} mm. {{bolt_diameter_assessment}}

title: Allowable Connection Load
learningObjectives: Calculate the allowable direct-shear load for a bolt group.
student: Determine the maximum total connection shear the bolt group can carry at the required factor of safety within this simplified model.

title: Engineering Assessment and Limitations
learningObjectives: Make a bounded engineering recommendation from a simplified connector check.
student: Give a concise engineering recommendation and identify at least two additional effects that must be checked before approving the real basketball-hoop connection.
instructor: {{bolt_engineering_assessment}} A complete design must also check effects such as eccentric bolt-group action and tension, plate bearing and tear-out, prying, threads at the shear plane, preload and slip, fatigue and impact dynamics, wall anchors, and actual bracket geometry.
gradingNotes: Do not award full credit for an unqualified claim that the complete real connection is safe.
